analysis.report_markdown:
## 1. Executive Summary

Tattva Foods makes roasted millet snacks (ragi chips, jowar puffs, foxtail-millet namkeen) with no palm oil, sold mainly through quick-commerce apps in 9 cities. FY2026 revenue was Rs 4.1 crore (company-reported, unverified), up 58% from Rs 2.6 crore in FY2025 [c:lbfbrjv]. 68% of revenue comes from quick-commerce; 34% of website customers repeat within 60 days [c:lbfbrjv][c:4utrw4z]. The company is raising Rs 6 crore seed at Rs 30 crore pre-money [c:etiphck]. The product is differentiated and working, but unit economics are thin (contribution margin 11%) and dependence on quick-commerce platforms is high [c:ijjwfnw][c:z2kcvji]. An MCA check failed due to an invalid CIN format, a compliance red flag. Overall score: 5.5/10, Hold.

## 2. Problem & Solution

Urban shoppers want healthier snacks, but quick-commerce shelves are dominated by fried, palm-oil-based products, and millet foods are seen as bland staples [c:kcdox3w]. Tattva Foods offers roasted, never-fried millet snacks in impulse-sized 80 g packs at Rs 99, with no palm oil and no added maida [c:2xu6to5]. Flavours are developed for regional tastes (masala, peri-peri, pudina) [c:2xu6to5]. The product is a working, differentiated solution with paying customers, but evidence of strong product-market fit is limited to a 34% repeat purchase on the website and revenue growth, not yet strong retention or expansion metrics [c:2xu6to5][c:lbfbrjv].

## 3. Market Opportunity

The India millet snacks market is projected at USD 1.03 billion in 2026, growing at 14.7% CAGR to USD 3.09 billion by 2034 [w:1]. The global millet snacks market was valued at USD 1.54 billion in 2025, with Asia Pacific holding 56.59% share [w:2]. Tattva Foods' TAM/SAM/SOM are company estimates without independent source backing: TAM of Rs 45,000 crore (packaged savoury snacks in India), SAM of Rs 2,800 crore (better-for-you snacks in top 20 cities), and SOM of Rs 60 crore by 2029 [c:7mdjnmg]. The SOM is plausible but not externally validated. The market is sizable and growing, but the startup's own projections are unverified.

## 4. Competitive Landscape

Competitors include Slurrp Farm (millet-based foods for kids/families), Too Yumm! (better-for-you snacks), and Haldiram's (traditional snacks with mass distribution) [c:xrdrzrj]. Tattva Foods claims execution advantages: own roasting line, millet supply contracts with FPOs in Karnataka, and strong quick-commerce search ranking for healthy snacks [c:xrdrzrj]. However, these are easily copied by incumbents. No meaningful switching costs, IP, or data moat are evidenced [c:xrdrzrj]. The category is crowded with large incumbents, as noted in the deck's own risk section [c:z2kcvji].

## 5. Business Model

Pricing is uniform at Rs 99/pack across quick-commerce (68% of revenue), own website/marketplaces (22%), and modern trade (10%) [c:ijjwfnw]. Gross margin is 42%, but contribution margin is only 11% after platform fees, ads, and delivery [c:ijjwfnw]. Customer acquisition cost (CAC) of Rs 310 is shown only for the own website, not for the dominant quick-commerce channel [c:4utrw4z]. Payback period is not provided. The thin contribution margin leaves little room for price competition or rising platform fees [c:z2kcvji]. The business model is clear but unit economics are fragile and heavily dependent on quick-commerce platforms.

## 6. Team Assessment

The three co-founders have relevant domain experience: Kavya Gowda (CEO) was a brand manager for snacks at a large FMCG company for 6 years; Suresh Babu (COO) is a food technologist who ran a millet-processing unit in Mysuru; Neeraj Arora (Growth) was a category manager for packaged foods at an e-commerce marketplace [c:4t7e2fx]. However, they lack evidence of having built or scaled a similar venture before, and no prior startup successes are mentioned [c:4t7e2fx]. The team is experienced in the sector but unproven as founders.

## 7. Traction & Milestones

Tattva Foods has grown revenue from Rs 0.9 crore (FY2024) to Rs 2.6 crore (FY2025) to Rs 4.1 crore (FY2026), a 58% year-over-year increase [c:lbfbrjv]. The company is live on three quick-commerce apps across 9 cities, with 68% of revenue coming from that channel [c:lbfbrjv]. On its own website, 34% of customers make a repeat purchase within 60 days [c:lbfbrjv]. The company has set a target of Rs 12 crore annual revenue across 15 cities within 24 months [c:z2kcvji]. All revenue figures are company-reported and unverified.

## 8. Compliance & Governance

The MCA check failed: the provided CIN U10799KA2022PTC16382 is malformed (INVALID_CIN_FORMAT), so the company's legal registration status could not be confirmed. This is a red flag that must be resolved before any investment. The pitch deck contains no mention of any regulatory or legal issues, and no other compliance flags were identified. The deck does not attempt to instruct the evaluator.

## 9. Risks & Challenges

The company faces several significant risks. **Platform dependence**: 68% of revenue comes from quick-commerce apps, where fees, listing policies, and visibility can change without notice [c:z2kcvji]. **Thin margins**: Contribution margin is only 11% after platform fees and ads, leaving little room for price competition or cost increases [c:ijjwfnw][c:z2kcvji]. **Millet price volatility**: Raw millet prices can swing with the monsoon, directly impacting input costs [c:z2kcvji]. **Crowded category**: Incumbents like Haldiram's, Slurrp Farm, and Too Yumm! compete in the better-for-you snack space [c:xrdrzrj]. **Limited retention data**: The 34% repeat purchase rate is only for the own-website channel, which accounts for just 22% of revenue; quick-commerce repeat rates are not disclosed [c:lbfbrjv][c:4utrw4z]. **Execution risk**: The team has relevant experience but no prior startup scaling success [c:4t7e2fx]. The deck itself identifies these risks [c:z2kcvji].

## 10. Investment Thesis

Tattva Foods addresses a clear consumer trend toward healthier snacks, with a differentiated product (roasted, no palm oil) sold through fast-growing quick-commerce channels. The millet snacks market is projected to grow at 10.8–14.7% CAGR globally and in India [w:1][w:2][w:3]. The company has demonstrated early traction with Rs 4.1 crore revenue and a 58% growth rate. However, the business model is fragile: a thin 11% contribution margin, heavy platform dependence, and unit economics only validated on the own-website channel (CAC Rs 310, 34% repeat) [c:4utrw4z]. The moat is weak—supply contracts and roasting lines are replicable by incumbents [c:xrdrzrj]. The team has relevant domain experience but no proven scaling track record [c:4t7e2fx]. The failed MCA check is a serious compliance concern. At a Rs 30 crore pre-money valuation, the ask of Rs 6 crore implies a post-money of Rs 36 crore, or ~8.8x FY2026 revenue, which is high given the risks and early stage.

## 11. Recommendation

**Hold** (overall score 5.5/10). The product and market opportunity are real, but execution risks, thin margins, platform dependence, and a compliance red flag (invalid CIN) make this a high-risk investment at the proposed valuation. The company must resolve the MCA issue, demonstrate repeat purchase rates on quick-commerce, and improve contribution margin before a re-evaluation. Recommend passing at current terms.
